specification.problem: Quantum pattern classification using a Trugenberger-style quantum measurement of Hamming distance between an input pattern and stored training patterns, illustrated on handwritten digit recognition from MNIST.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction only: the problem statement and a minimal finite-instance Hamming-distance encoding. Circuit details, measurement protocol and MNIST encoding are not given in the abstract; the circuit, measurement and postprocessing are assumed templates.

specification.initial_state: Assumed: input register in |x>, memory register in |M> (uniform superposition of training patterns), control qubit in |0>.

steps.description: Prepare memory register in uniform superposition of the N stored binary training patterns, and load the input pattern x into the input register.

Apply Hadamard to the control qubit, then compute bitwise differences between input and memory registers (XOR-type operations) so each branch carries the Hamming distance (assumed Trugenberger-style; details not in abstract).
Apply a distance-dependent phase on the control qubit branch, then a final Hadamard on the control qubit so that the control-qubit outcome probability depends on d_H (assumed).

specification.measurement: Assumed: measure the control qubit in the computational basis, post-selecting on the outcome favoring small d_H; then measure the memory register (and its class label) to read out a stored pattern, with probability weighted toward patterns near x. Repeat over many shots.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: tally the class labels of the retrieved patterns over repeated runs and assign the input the majority (most frequent) class label. Exact decision rule not in the abstract.
assumptions: Circuit steps follow a generic Trugenberger-style control-qubit interference template as an assumption; the abstract does not specify gates
